# Daily Digest for Muki — Issue #099 Research Dossier

**Date:** 2026-11-19  
**Search Window Used:** 14 days (expanded from 24h/7d to cover active exhibitions and papers released between late October and mid-November 2026)  
**Editor’s Pick Lead Candidate:** Signal 3 (Mori Art Museum — *Mariko Mori: All That Shines*)

---

### Candidate 1: Feminist Structure Signal

* **Proposed Headline (CN):** 维也纳 Belvedere 21 开幕《Feminist Futures Forever》：以 238 位艺术家作品重构 40 年女性主义艺术脉络
* **Original English Title:** Belvedere 21 Opens 'Feminist Futures Forever': 238 Artists Re-examine 40 Years of Feminist Art Histories
* **Source URL:** `https://www.belvedere.at/en/press/feminist-futures-forever`
* **Publication / Opening Date:** 2026-11-05 (on view through 2027-03-08)
* **Verified Facts:**
  * Curated by Christiane Erharter and Stefanie Reisinger at Belvedere 21 in Vienna.
  * Re-examines the landmark 1985 exhibition *Kunst mit Eigen-Sinn* (Art with a Mind of Its Own), taking place in the exact same building.
  * Features 238 international artists across generations, including Marina Abramović, Leiko Ikemura, VALIE EXPORT, Barbara Hammer, Birgit Jürgenssen, Yoko Ono, Cindy Sherman, Rosemarie Trockel, and Sophie Calle.
  * Organized across nine thematic sections addressing structural inequality in patriarchal societies, spanning labor, reproduction, the body, public space, identity, and memory.
* **Relevance to Muki:** Demonstrates how major contemporary art institutions re-evaluate historic feminist avant-garde exhibitions, expanding binary art histories into multi-vocal networks of body, labor, and public space.
* **Duplication & Status Assessment:** Follow-up (Institutional tracking of Belvedere 21, following the Maria Hahnenkamp solo exhibition in Issue 2026-11-15).

### Candidate 2: Visual Culture Signal

* **Proposed Headline (CN):** Foam 摄影博物馆举办基尔塔纳·库纳斯个展《Not What You Saw》：以南印度女性健美者的身体与日常打破范式
* **Original English Title:** Foam Presents Keerthana Kunnath's 'Not What You Saw': Female Bodybuilders in South India Challenge Gender Norms
* **Source URL:** `https://www.foam.org/events/keerthana-kunnath`
* **Publication / Opening Date:** 2026-09-18 (exhibition on view through 2026-11-27)
* **Verified Facts:**
  * First museum solo exhibition of London-based Indian photographer Keerthana Kunnath at Foam 3h in Amsterdam.
  * The series *Not What You Saw* documents over a dozen female bodybuilders in Kerala, South India.
  * Juxtaposes physical muscular strength with soft, warm sunset lighting and lush domestic backdrops.
  * Tracks athletes across home life, community relationships, and regional competitions, highlighting the emotional, physical, and financial strain behind their choice of discipline.
* **Relevance to Muki:** Combines feminist visual culture, documentary photography, and non-Western body politics. Demonstrates how image-making can document physical labor while challenging normative beauty standards.
* **Duplication & Status Assessment:** New signal.

### Candidate 3: China / East Asia Signal (Editor’s Pick Candidate)

* **Proposed Headline (CN):** 森美术馆开幕森万里子回顾展《All That Shines》：30 年跨媒介创作与脑电交互装置
* **Original English Title:** Mori Art Museum Opens Mariko Mori Retrospective 'All That Shines': 30 Years of Cross-Media Practice and Bio-Feedback Tech
* **Source URL:** `https://www.mori.art.museum/en/exhibitions/marikomori/index.html`
* **Publication / Opening Date:** 2026-10-31 (on view through 2027-03-28; reviewed Nov 2026)
* **Verified Facts:**
  * Co-organized by Mori Art Museum (Tokyo) and Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum (New York), co-curated by Mami Kataoka and Alexandra Munroe.
  * Mori's first major Japan retrospective in over 20 years, bringing together 40 works spanning performance photography, video, computer graphics, and large installations.
  * Re-examines her 1990s "Cyborg" series of performance photography alongside sci-fi imagery and animist/Buddhist cosmologies.
  * Highlights *Wave UFO* (1999–2002), an interactive pod that visualizes real-time brainwave bio-feedback into visual graphics and sound for three participants at a time.
  * Features the title artwork *All That Shines* (2026), created with technical support from Anthropic's Claude AI team.
* **Relevance to Muki:** Directly connects East Asian visual culture, feminist cyborg body history (1990s identity photography), media archaeology (bio-feedback hardware), and AI-native creative technology.
* **Duplication & Status Assessment:** New signal.

### Candidate 4: AI Research / Creative Tech Signal

* **Proposed Headline (CN):** 研究团队提出 MAPE 框架：以程序演化自动化设计与优化 AI Agent 动态记忆架构
* **Original English Title:** Researchers Introduce MAPE: Program Evolution for Automated Discovery of AI Agent Memory Architectures
* **Source URL:** `https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05339`
* **Publication Date:** 2026-11-12
* **Verified Facts:**
  * Developed by researchers at the University of Minnesota and collaborating institutions (Xinheng Ding et al.).
  * Introduces MAPE, an automated program evolution framework that searches over complete LLM agent memory designs.
  * Uses a standardized lifecycle interface and an iterative diagnosis-proposal loop to revise memory building, retrieval, and context preparation.
  * Demonstrates that retaining raw conversation history alongside extracted notes recovers critical missing details, and query-routed scaffolding organizes evidence based on question intent before answering.
  * Achieves up to a 12% accuracy gain over human-designed memory baselines on LoCoMo and LongMemEval while reducing serving costs by 65%.
* **Relevance to Muki:** Addresses memory management in AI agents. Shows how separating raw record preservation from query-time evidence structure improves persistent context and knowledge management workflows.
* **Duplication & Status Assessment:** Follow-up (AI Agent long-horizon memory framework line of research).

### Candidate 5: Archive / Long Read / Opportunity

* **Proposed Headline (CN):** Black Women Photographers 联合尼康启动 2026 第四季度资助：提供 2500 美元现金与 Z6III 镜头套机
* **Original English Title:** Black Women Photographers and Nikon Launch Q4 2026 Grant Call: $2,500 Cash and Camera Equipment
* **Source URL:** `https://blackwomenphotographers.com/nikon-grant-fund`
* **Publication Date:** 2026-11-01 (Deadline: 2026-11-20)
* **Verified Facts:**
  * Open call hosted by the global collective Black Women Photographers (BWP) in partnership with Nikon.
  * Deadline for Q4 2026 applications is November 20, 2026 (11:59 PM ET).
  * Open to Black women and non-binary photographers worldwide; entry is free.
  * Recipient receives a $2,500 USD cash grant and a Nikon Z6III camera kit with a 24-70mm f/4 lens.
* **Relevance to Muki:** A current, high-quality, actionable opportunity directly serving marginalized women and non-binary visual storytellers, supporting independent photography production and equipment infrastructure.
* **Duplication & Status Assessment:** New signal.
